newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican cold front seen skirting north coffee belt.
newsitem.headline: Mexican cold front seen skirting north coffee belt.

text.p: A cold front fuelled by a southerly-moving mass of polar air entered over north Mexico Wednesday and is seen skirting the country's most northerly coffee belt Thursday and Friday, meteorologists predicted.
"It is coming from the United States and is bringing much lower temperatures than usual," a weather forecaster for TV network Televisa said Wednesday.
Temperatures of -7 degrees celsius were seen overnight in Chihuahua City and Ciudad Juarez, Televisa said. Both cities are close to the U.S. border and distant from coffee zones.

But forecasts are for the cold front to edge further south in the next two days toward Mexico's most northerly coffee belt - the mountains of the state of Veracruz and in the northern Sierra of the state of Puebla.

Traditionally, these two neighbouring states are the ones most threatened by cold weather in Mexico. Both have coffee growing at high altitudes and are among the most northerly plantations in the Americas.
Temperatures given Wednesday for cities close to the belt included Toluca at 4 degrees celsius, Puebla at 6 degrees celsius and Oaxaca at 7 degrees celsius, Televisa said.
Reforma newspaper predicted that temperatures would continue to decline through Thursday reaching a minimum of 0 degree celsius in Mexico City from a minimum Wednesday morning of 2 degrees celsius.
Those forecasts are in line with predictions from other meterologists.

Smith Barney meterologist Jon Davis said Tuesday in his daily update that there is "potential for some damage" in some sections of the Mexican coffee belt. He predicted the two coldest mornings will be Thursday and Friday, especially at high elevations in the most northerly parts of the belt.

The National Meterological Service said Wednesday in its daily bulletin it expected snowfalls overnight Wednesday-Thursday in central mountains (non-coffee growing zones) and sharp frosts in the states of Coahuila, Chihuahua, Durango, the State of Mexico, Jalisco and Sonora.
"The cold front will also bring rains to the (coffee growing states of) Tabasco, Veracruz, Chiapas, Oaxaca, Puebla and San Luis Potosi," the service said.
Frosts or near-freezing weather in mid-December is fairly unusual in Mexico. The lowest temperatures of the winter are normally recorded in early January.

Last winter, several cold fronts threatened the Mexican coffee crop in Veracruz and Puebla. In the end, only light touches of frost hit the exposed pockets of the crop at high altitudes. Damage was minimal to beans and trees.
Indeed, Veracruz produced a record 1.7 million 60-kg bags of coffee last 1995-1996 cycle, usurping Chiapas as the biggest producer state.
--Chris Aspin, Mexico City newsroom (525) 7289530. E-mail at chris.aspin@reuters.com
